summary.text: The complex plane is a flat grid where each complex number is a point, with the real numbers along the horizontal axis and the imaginary numbers along the vertical axis.
Complex numbers add on this plane like vectors, and multiplying two of them multiplies their sizes while adding their angles.
Multiplying by a complex number whose size is exactly one acts as a pure rotation.

facts.label: Other names
facts.value: The Argand plane or the Gauss plane

facts.label: First described by
facts.value: Caspar Wessel, though the diagram is named after Argand

facts.label: Positive direction
facts.value: Counterclockwise is the conventional positive direction around a curve

facts.label: Point at infinity
facts.value: Adding one extra point gives the extended complex plane

items.prompt: You plot a complex number whose real part is 3 and whose imaginary part is 2. From the origin, how do you move to its spot?

options.label: Two steps along the real axis, then three up
Three steps straight up the page, then two across
Three steps along the real axis, then two up
Five steps along a single diagonal

items.explain: The horizontal axis holds the real numbers and the vertical axis holds the imaginary numbers.

items.prompt: When two complex numbers are added on the plane, which ordinary operation does the result mimic?

options.label: Adding two vectors
Multiplying two lengths
Averaging the two points
Keeping the longer arrow

items.explain: Under addition, complex numbers add like vectors.

items.prompt: On the complex plane, one number has size 2 and angle 30 degrees, another has size 3 and angle 40 degrees. What are the size and angle of their product?

options.label: Size 5, angle 70 degrees
Size 6, angle 1,200 degrees
Size 1.5, angle 10 degrees
Size 6, angle 70 degrees

items.explain: The size of a product is the product of the sizes, and the angle of a product is the sum of the angles.

items.prompt: Which kind of complex number should you multiply by if you want every point to turn around without any stretching or shrinking?

options.label: Any number whose real part is positive
A number whose absolute value is 1
Any number lying on the imaginary axis
A real number larger than 1

items.explain: Multiplying sizes leaves a size of 1 unchanged, and the angles add, so multiplication by a number of modulus 1 acts as a rotation.

items.prompt: The plane is wrapped onto a sphere by drawing a straight line from each point to the north pole. Where does a point very near the origin end up?

options.label: In the northern hemisphere, near the north pole
On the equator, along the unit circle
In the southern hemisphere, near the south pole
At the north pole itself

items.explain: The origin goes to the south pole, and the whole interior of the unit circle lands on the southern hemisphere.

items.prompt: On the sphere picture, the north pole has no partner in the plane. How is the one-to-one match completed?

options.label: One extra point, the point at infinity, joins the plane
The north pole is moved down onto the origin
Two points of the plane are glued together
The equator is cut out of the sphere

items.explain: The point at infinity is added to the plane and identified with the north pole, giving the extended complex plane.
